request.subject: Can Wolves Really Change Rivers? - part 2: The Wolves Come Home
request.title: Can Wolves Really Change Rivers? (Part 2/3)
request.description:
Wolves returned to Yellowstone, elk numbers fell and beavers came back. It became a famous comeback story. Would you have brought them back?

Part 2 of 3: Can Wolves Really Change Rivers?

Sources:
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_wolves_in_Yellowstone
https://www.nps.gov/articles/the-big-scientific-debate-trophic-cascades.htm
https://www.spokesman.com/stories/2024/apr/07/yellowstone-research-reignites-debate-over-wolf-ge/

Stock footage: Pexels. Made with AI-assisted narration.

#shorts #truestory

extra_params.video_script: Fourteen wolves from Canada were set free in Yellowstone. In Part 1, people wiped out the park's wolves by the late 1920s. The first wolves arrived in 1995, and more followed a year later. The wolves hunted elk, and elk numbers fell sharply. Scientists reported willows and aspens growing taller in places. Beaver colonies grew from one to nine in about a decade. It became one of the most famous comeback stories in nature. But the wolves weren't the only hunters killing Yellowstone's elk. Subscribe so you don't miss Part 3.
